messages.author: 2bcecdd9c0443e65
messages.subject: Leap years in ectotherm model
parts:
Hi Mike,

Does ectotherm() keep track of leap years? I'm currently testing with micro_usa, see example for year 2016 below. I don't see an argument for ectotherm() to specify leap years or corresponding date handling, is this a bug or intended behavior?

I can easily just overwrite the dates of the output `ecto` objects with the correct leap year dates, but thought I should ask.

Thanks,
Dave


library(NicheMapR)

# Run micro_usa for example location and time period in the function documentation
micro <- micro_usa(loc = c(-117.8919161, 36.582016), dstart = "01/01/2016", dfinish = "31/12/2016")

# Run ectotherm model with all defaults
ecto <- ectotherm()

# Microclimate model correctly displays 366 days in year 2016
shadmet = as.data.frame(micro$shadmet)
max(shadmet$DOY) # 366

# Ectotherm output only displays 365 days
environ = as.data.frame(ecto$environ)
max(environ$DOY) # 365
tail(environ) # Assigns days 366 to DOY 1, codes YEAR as 1 again

--
David Klinges, PhD

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Leap years in ectotherm model
parts:
Hi Dave,

You're right - it doesn't account for leap years. I hadn't realised that so thanks for pointing it out. It still does all the days in the microclimate output but the internal yearly summarising that the ectotherm model does will be out if leap years are involved. Leap years are a pain! I had a quick look at the code structure and it will take me a while to correct this but, as you say, you can just overwrite the DOY in the ectotherm output with the DOY in the microclimate output.

All the best,
Mike

messages.author: 2bcecdd9c0443e65
messages.subject: Re: Leap years in ectotherm model
parts:
Hi Mike,

Good to know. I only caught this from modeling over a 45-year time series, which ended up with some significant drift in what ectotherm() thinks the DOY is. But yes for most purposes I suppose the impact is limited, as all of the important time series info is inherited from `micro` anyways. So I imagine most users can overwrite DOY from micro (which is what I'll do).

It might be useful for users to add a quick note about this small issue in the ectotherm() function documentation (perhaps with the `nyears` argument description?)

Best,
Dave
ᐧ
